q: The headquarters of the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) is located at:
e: RDSO, the research and standards organisation of Indian Railways which frames technical specifications and standards, has its headquarters at Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh.

q: The Integral Coach Factory (ICF) is located at:
e: The Integral Coach Factory at Perambur, Chennai, manufactures passenger coaches, including the train sets and coaches turned out for Indian Railways since its setting up in 1955.

q: The first railway in India, in 1853, ran between:
e: The first railway in India ran between Bombay (Bori Bunder) and Thane on 16 April 1853, covering about 34 km, marking the start of rail transport in the country.

q: Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) primarily functions as:

options.A: The catering arm of Indian Railways
options.B: The dedicated market-borrowing and financing arm of Indian Railways
options.C: The construction company of Indian Railways
options.D: The telecom arm of Indian Railways

e: IRFC is the dedicated financing arm of Indian Railways; it borrows funds from the capital market to finance rolling stock and other railway assets, which are then leased to the Railways.

q: The Rail Coach Factory (RCF) is located at:
e: The Rail Coach Factory is situated at Kapurthala in Punjab, where it manufactures modern passenger coaches, including LHB coaches.

q: Chittaranjan Locomotive Works (CLW) is located at:
e: Chittaranjan Locomotive Works is located at Chittaranjan in West Bengal and is a major production unit manufacturing electric locomotives for Indian Railways.

q: The Banaras Locomotive Works (BLW), formerly Diesel Locomotive Works, is located at:
e: Banaras Locomotive Works (formerly Diesel Locomotive Works) is at Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh; it was renamed when its production focus shifted from diesel to electric locomotives.

q: The Modern Coach Factory (MCF) is located at:
e: The Modern Coach Factory is located at Raebareli (Lalganj) in Uttar Pradesh and produces modern LHB-design passenger coaches.

q: Rail Wheel Factory (RWF) is located at:
e: The Rail Wheel Factory at Yelahanka, Bengaluru, manufactures wheels, axles and wheel sets for Indian Railways.

q: The Patiala Locomotive Works (PLW) is situated in which State?
e: Patiala Locomotive Works (formerly Diesel Loco Modernisation Works) is at Patiala, which is in the State of Punjab.

q: The headquarters of North Eastern Railway is at:
e: North Eastern Railway, formed mainly out of the old Oudh Tirhut and Assam Railway systems, has its headquarters at Gorakhpur in Uttar Pradesh.

q: The headquarters of South Central Railway is at:
e: South Central Railway, with headquarters at Secunderabad (Rail Nilayam), serves Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and adjoining regions.

q: The headquarters of Western Railway is at:
e: Western Railway has its headquarters at Mumbai (Churchgate), and operates the busy Mumbai suburban network and lines into Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.

q: The headquarters of East Central Railway is at:
e: East Central Railway, created in the zone reorganisation of 2002, has its headquarters at Hajipur in Bihar.

q: The headquarters of North Western Railway is at:
e: North Western Railway, also formed in 2002, has its headquarters at Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan.

q: The headquarters of South Western Railway is at:
e: South Western Railway has its headquarters at Hubballi in Karnataka, though Bengaluru is the biggest traffic centre of the zone.

q: The full form of IRCON is:

options.B: Indian Railway Corporation of India Limited

e: IRCON stands for Indian Railway Construction Company Limited, the railway PSU executing construction projects in India and abroad; it is now known as Ircon International Limited.

q: Which organisation looks after the catering and tourism services of Indian Railways, including the operation of trains like Bharat Gaurav?
e: IRCTC, the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation, handles catering, online ticketing and tourism services, including the Bharat Gaurav tourist trains.

q: CONCOR is primarily engaged in:
e: CONCOR, the Container Corporation of India, runs container terminals and moves EXIM and domestic container traffic by rail and road.

q: In railway computerisation, the full form of FOIS is:
e: FOIS, the Freight Operations Information System, is the computer system used by Indian Railways for monitoring and managing freight operations, including wagon and rake movements.

q: PRS, the computerised reservation system of Indian Railways, stands for:
e: PRS stands for Passenger Reservation System, the computerised network through which reserved train tickets are booked across India.

q: UTS, used for booking unreserved tickets, stands for:
e: UTS stands for Unreserved Ticketing System, used for issuing unreserved (general) tickets, including through mobile and counter channels.

q: CORE, headquartered at Allahabad (Prayagraj), is primarily responsible for:
e: CORE, the Central Organisation for Railway Electrification, headquartered at Prayagraj, plans and executes railway electrification works across the country.

q: DFCCIL is associated with the development of:
e: DFCCIL, the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited, builds and operates the Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors for high-speed goods trains.

q: RITES Limited primarily provides:

options.B: Transport infrastructure consultancy and engineering services

e: RITES Limited is a Government of India enterprise providing consultancy, engineering and project services for transport infrastructure, in India and overseas.

q: RailTel Corporation of India Limited primarily provides:

options.B: Telecom and network services using railway right of way

e: RailTel provides broadband, telecom and network services using the optical fibre network laid along railway tracks and the railway right of way.

q: The Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS) is located at:
e: CRIS, the Centre for Railway Information Systems, which designs and runs the Railways' IT applications like PRS and FOIS, is located at Chanakyapuri, New Delhi.

q: Which of the following heritage railways of India is NOT inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list?
e: The Darjeeling, Nilgiri and Kalka-Shimla railways together form the UNESCO-listed "Mountain Railways of India"; the Matheran Hill Railway is only on the tentative list, so it is not inscribed.

q: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway is famous by the popular name:
e: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, the narrow-gauge line running between New Jalpaiguri and Darjeeling since 1881, is popularly called the Toy Train.

q: The Konkan Railway line runs along the west coast of India, connecting Roha in Maharashtra with:
e: The Konkan Railway runs along the west coast from Roha in Maharashtra to Thokur near Mangaluru, passing through Goa and coastal Karnataka.

q: The book 'Discovery of India' was written by:
e: "The Discovery of India" was written by Jawaharlal Nehru during his imprisonment at Ahmednagar Fort in 1944-46 and traces India's history and culture.

q: 'Wings of Fire' is the autobiography of:

options.A: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam

e: "Wings of Fire" is the autobiography of Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, the aerospace scientist who later became President of India.

q: The book 'Gitanjali' was written by:
e: "Gitanjali", the celebrated collection of devotional poems by Rabindranath Tagore, won him the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.

q: Who wrote the famous novel 'Guide'?
e: "Guide" (1958), the story of Raju the tour guide, is the best-known novel of R. K. Narayan, creator of the fictional town of Malgudi.

q: The telephone was invented by:
e: The telephone was patented in 1876 by Alexander Graham Bell, who is credited with its invention and the first practical telephone call.

q: The theory of evolution by natural selection was propounded by:
e: Charles Darwin propounded evolution by natural selection in his 1859 work "On the Origin of Species".

q: Penicillin was discovered by:
e: Penicillin, the first widely used antibiotic, was discovered in 1928 by Alexander Fleming from the Penicillium mould.

q: A 'Sphygmomanometer' is an instrument used to measure:
e: A sphygmomanometer is the cuff-based instrument used by doctors to measure blood pressure.

q: A 'Seismograph' is used to measure:
e: A seismograph records the intensity and duration of earthquakes by detecting seismic waves passing through the earth.

q: An 'Altimeter' in an aircraft measures:
e: An altimeter in an aircraft measures altitude, i.e. the height of the aircraft above sea level, using atmospheric pressure.

q: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur and:
e: In the First Battle of Panipat in 1526, Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, the last Sultan of Delhi, and founded the Mughal Empire in India.

q: The Battle of Plassey (1757), which laid the foundation of British rule in India, was fought in present-day:
e: The Battle of Plassey in 1757, where Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah, was fought at Plassey in present-day West Bengal, laying the foundation of British rule.

q: Who was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal?
e: Karnam Malleswari won a bronze medal in weightlifting at the Sydney Olympics of 2000, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal.

q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian States?
e: The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight Indian States: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

q: Which is the longest river flowing entirely within India?
e: The Godavari, about 1,465 km long and often called Dakshin Ganga, is the longest river lying entirely within India; the Ganga system is longer overall but flows on into Bangladesh.

q: The 'Sarkaria Commission' was set up to examine:
e: The Sarkaria Commission, headed by Justice R. S. Sarkaria and set up in 1983, was appointed to examine and review Centre-State relations.

q: The Finance Commission of India is constituted under which Article of the Constitution?
e: The Finance Commission, the body that recommends the sharing of taxes between the Centre and the States every five years, is constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution.

q: The Committee that recommended the concept of the Railway Budget being merged with the General Budget was chaired by:
e: The merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget from 2017-18 was recommended by the committee headed by Bibek Debroy on restructuring and resource mobilisation for Railways.

q: The Kakodkar Committee (2012) was associated with:
e: The Kakodkar Committee of 2012 was the High Level Safety Review Committee, set up to review and recommend improvements in railway safety.

q: India's national song 'Vande Mataram' was composed by:
e: "Vande Mataram", India's national song, was composed by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee and appears in his novel "Anandamath".

q: The headquarters of Northern Railway is at:
e: Northern Railway, the largest zone by route length among the older zones, has its headquarters at Baroda House, New Delhi.

q: The headquarters of Southern Railway is at:
e: Southern Railway has its headquarters at Chennai in Tamil Nadu, serving the southern States.

q: The headquarters of Central Railway is at:
e: Central Railway has its headquarters at Mumbai, functioning from Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus.

q: The headquarters of North East Frontier Railway is at:
e: Northeast Frontier Railway has its headquarters at Maligaon in Guwahati, Assam, and serves the north-eastern States.

q: The headquarters of East Coast Railway is at:
e: East Coast Railway, carved out mainly from South Eastern Railway, has its headquarters at Bhubaneswar, the capital of Odisha.

q: The headquarters of West Central Railway is at:
e: West Central Railway, formed in 2003, has its headquarters at Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh.

q: The headquarters of South East Central Railway is at:
e: South East Central Railway, another zone created in 2003, has its headquarters at Bilaspur in Chhattisgarh.

q: The headquarters of North Central Railway is at:
e: North Central Railway has its headquarters at Prayagraj (Allahabad) in Uttar Pradesh.

q: The first Rajdhani Express, introduced in 1969, ran between:
e: The first Rajdhani Express was introduced in 1969 between New Delhi and Howrah, cutting the journey time between the capital and Calcutta.

q: The first Shatabdi Express, introduced in 1988, ran between:
e: The first Shatabdi Express was introduced in 1988 between New Delhi and Jhansi as a fast intercity day train; it was later extended to Bhopal.

q: The first Metro railway in India, which began operations in 1984, was started in:
e: India's first metro service began in Kolkata in 1984 with the Esplanade-Bhowanipore stretch of the Kolkata Metro.

q: The official mascot of Indian Railways is:
e: Bholu, the cheerful elephant dressed as a railway guard holding a signal lamp, is the official mascot of Indian Railways.

q: The National Rail Museum is located at:
e: The National Rail Museum, displaying historic locomotives and coaches, is located at Chanakyapuri in New Delhi.

q: On the recommendation of the Acworth Committee, the Railway Budget was separated from the General Budget in the year:
e: On the recommendation of the Acworth Committee, the Separation Convention of 1924 separated railway finances from general finances, and a separate Railway Budget followed from 1925.

q: Who was the first Railway Minister of independent India?
e: John Mathai, an economist, was the first Railway Minister of independent India in the Nehru cabinet.

q: The National Academy of Indian Railways (NAIR) is located at:
e: The National Academy of Indian Railways at Vadodara, formerly the Railway Staff College, is the apex training institute for railway officers.

q: The Indian Railways Institute of Signal Engineering and Telecommunications (IRISET) is located at:
e: IRISET, the Indian Railways Institute of Signal Engineering and Telecommunications, is located at Secunderabad and trains officers in signalling and telecom subjects.

q: The full form of RVNL is:
e: RVNL stands for Rail Vikas Nigam Limited, the PSU that executes railway infrastructure projects such as new lines and doubling.

q: The National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) is implementing:

options.D: Complete electrification of broad gauge routes

e: NHSRCL is implementing India's first high-speed rail (bullet train) corridor between Mumbai and Ahmedabad using Japanese Shinkansen technology.

q: 'KAVACH', developed indigenously for Indian Railways, is a:
e: KAVACH is the indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection system that applies brakes automatically to prevent collisions and signal passing at danger.

q: The Konkan Railway was constructed under the leadership of:
e: The Konkan Railway, one of India's toughest rail engineering projects through the Western Ghats, was built under the leadership of E. Sreedharan, its first Chairman and Managing Director.

q: The headquarters of the Konkan Railway Corporation Limited is at:
e: The headquarters of Konkan Railway Corporation Limited is at Belapur in Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra.

q: The National Rail Plan (Vision 2030) aims to increase the modal share of Railways in freight movement to about:
e: The National Rail Plan (Vision 2030) aims to raise the share of Railways in freight movement to about 45 per cent by 2030.

q: Surekha Yadav is known as the first woman to work as a ______ on Indian Railways.
e: Surekha Yadav, who joined in 1988 and drove trains including the Deccan Queen, is recognised as the first woman loco pilot (train driver) of Indian Railways.

q: The first woman Railway Minister of India was:
e: Mamata Banerjee, who first held the Railway Ministry in 1999, was the first woman Railway Minister of India.

q: The word 'Secular' was added to the Preamble of the Constitution by the:
e: The words "Socialist", "Secular" and "Integrity" were inserted into the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment of 1976.

q: The Fundamental Rights are contained in which Part of the Indian Constitution?
e: Fundamental Rights, enforceable by the courts, are set out in Part III of the Constitution (Articles 12 to 35).

q: Panchayati Raj institutions were given constitutional status by the:
e: The 73rd Amendment of 1992 gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions and added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution.

q: Who was the first President of India?
e: Dr. Rajendra Prasad, who had chaired the Constituent Assembly, became the first President of India in 1950.

q: In the Third Battle of Panipat (1761), the Marathas were defeated by:
e: In the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761, the Maratha army was defeated by Ahmad Shah Abdali (Ahmad Shah Durrani) of Afghanistan.

q: The Battle of Haldighati (1576) is associated with:
e: The Battle of Haldighati of 1576 is remembered for Maharana Pratap of Mewar, who fought the Mughal forces of Akbar led by Man Singh.

q: The Quit India Movement was launched in the year:
e: The Quit India Movement, demanding an immediate end to British rule, was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in August 1942 with the call "Do or Die".

q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in the year:
e: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919 at Amritsar, where General Dyer's troops fired on an unarmed crowd.

q: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by:
e: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A. O. Hume, a retired British civil servant; its first session was held at Bombay under W. C. Bonnerjee.

q: Which is the longest river of India?
e: The Ganga, about 2,525 km long from the Himalayas to the Bay of Bengal, is the longest river of India.

q: Which is the largest State of India by area?
e: Rajasthan is India's largest State by area, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

q: The Hirakud Dam is built across the river:
e: The Hirakud Dam, one of the longest dams in the world, is built across the Mahanadi river in Odisha.

q: The 'Panchatantra' was composed by:
e: The "Panchatantra", the ancient collection of animal fables teaching life lessons, is traditionally attributed to the scholar Vishnu Sharma.

q: The famous novel 'Godan' was written by:
e: "Godan" (1936), considered the greatest Hindi novel, depicting the life of the peasant Hori, was written by Munshi Premchand.

q: The vaccine for smallpox was developed by:
e: Edward Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine in 1796, using cowpox material, laying the foundation of immunology.

q: The improved steam engine that powered the Industrial Revolution was developed by:
e: James Watt's improved steam engine, with a separate condenser, greatly increased efficiency and powered the Industrial Revolution.

q: An 'Anemometer' is an instrument used to measure:
e: An anemometer measures the speed of wind and is commonly seen at weather stations and airports.

q: The first Indian to travel into space was:
e: Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian in space in 1984, flying aboard the Soviet Soyuz T-11 to the Salyut 7 space station.

q: The 'White Revolution' in India is associated with the increase in:
e: The White Revolution, driven by Operation Flood under Dr. Verghese Kurien, made India the world's largest producer of milk.

q: The Dronacharya Award is given to:

options.A: The best sportsperson of the year

e: The Dronacharya Award, named after the guru of the Kuru princes, honours outstanding coaches in sports and games.

q: The headquarters of Eastern Railway is located at:
e: Eastern Railway, one of the oldest zones, has its headquarters at Fairlie Place, Kolkata.

q: The Indian Railways Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering (IRIMEE) is located at:
e: IRIMEE, the Indian Railways Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, is located at Jamalpur in Bihar.

q: The broad gauge used by Indian Railways has a track width of:
e: Indian broad gauge has a track width of 1,676 mm (5 feet 6 inches), wider than the 1,435 mm standard gauge used in most countries.

q: Project Unigauge of Indian Railways relates to:

options.A: Introduction of a uniform fare structure across all zones
options.B: Single-window clearance of all railway projects
options.C: Conversion of metre gauge and narrow gauge lines into broad gauge

e: Project Unigauge, launched in 1992, aims at converting metre gauge and narrow gauge routes into a uniform broad gauge network.

q: The first electric train service in India was introduced in 1925 between:
e: India's first electric train ran in 1925 between Bombay (Victoria Terminus) and Kurla on the Harbour line.
